Analysis: Hypothesis 1 presents a mechanistic framework that builds on well-established gut–liver interactions, utilizing multi-omics profiling to pinpoint microbial alterations and link them to inflammation and HCC progression. Its strength lies in a clear, plausible chain of events that is easier to experimentally control and validate. Hypothesis 2, while incorporating a novel digital health component with AI-driven real-time monitoring and personalized prebiotic interventions, introduces significant complexity. This increases challenges in integration, precise measurement, and operational safety. Although Hypothesis 2 is more innovative, its added complexity affects plausibility and testability compared to the more straightforward, safer approach of Hypothesis 1.
